title: Maintain an in-memory inventory with validated stock changes
prompt: Implement assertSku, assertQuantity, and the Inventory class in src/validation.js and src/inventory.js, then re-export assertSku, assertQuantity, and Inventory from src/index.js. Use ES modules and only Node built-ins. A valid SKU is a non-empty string with no leading or trailing whitespace and is case-sensitive; return it unchanged. A valid quantity is a positive safe integer. Both validators return the valid value and throw an Error otherwise. new Inventory(initial = []) accepts an array of { sku, quantity } entries, validates each, and sums duplicate SKUs; it must not mutate the initial array or its entries. add(sku, quantity) adds to existing stock or creates it and returns the new total. remove(sku, quantity) throws if the SKU is absent or stock is insufficient, otherwise subtracts, deletes the SKU when its stock reaches zero, and returns the remaining quantity. get(sku) returns the current quantity or 0 for a valid unknown SKU. list() returns a new array of fresh { sku, quantity } objects for positive stock entries, sorted ascending by SKU using JavaScript string comparison. Internal state must be private: changing objects returned by list() must not affect the store, and list() must return a new array each time. Reject non-array initial data and malformed entries with an Error.
